newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU airlines post 4.8 pct traffic rise in July.
newsitem.headline: EU airlines post 4.8 pct traffic rise in July.

text.p: West European airlines posted 4.8 percent growth in passenger traffic year-on-year in July, down from the eight percent average monthly mark registered so far in 1996, the Association of European Airlines said on Tuesday.

"Both European and North Atlantic services registered a 4.1 percent increase, with Far Eastern services doing slightly better at plus 6.4 percent," the AEA said in a statement. The AEA comprises all the region's major flag carriers.

"For almost all operating regions, capacity growth exceeded the traffic increase, leading to a 1.5-point drop in load factor to 74.6 percent - the first time since 1993 that July loads have failed to fill three-quarters of the aircraft seats.

"Cargo results showed a 3.2 percent increase overall with a 2.5 percent drop in traffic on the North Atlantic and an increase of 2.6 percent on Asian markets resulting also in a below-par capacity utilisation," the AEA said.

"The July results are a clear indicator that overcapacity is back with us. At the time of year when passenger demand is greatest, we should not be seeing so many empty seats," AEA secretary-general Karl-Heinz Neumeister said in the statement.
